title: Revolutions: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the language of revolutions and the three biggest of the modern era.
meta_desc: GCSE History Revolutions foundations — American, French and Russian revolutions vocab.
final_note: You learned the core vocabulary and key dates of the three big revolutions.

concepts.def: Sudden, fundamental change in government or society
A state where power lies with elected representatives
France's pre-1789 monarchy and noble order
Lenin's communist faction — seized power in 1917
Russian emperor — last was Nicholas II

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thirteen British colonies in North America rebelled over taxes and 'no taxation without representation'.

The Declaration of Independence in 1776 proclaimed a free republic. With French help, the colonies won independence by 1783.

France was bankrupt and unequal. The Estates-General met in 1789. On 14 July 1789 Parisians stormed the Bastille prison.

King Louis XVI was executed in January 1793. Then came the Reign of Terror and finally Napoleon.

WWI brought hunger and defeat. In February 1917, strikes forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate.

In October 1917 the Bolsheviks, led by Lenin, seized power. They made peace with Germany and built the world's first communist state.
